aqua.e: From Middle English aqua (“water”), borrowed from Latin aqua. Perhaps also a learned borrowing directly from Latin. Doublet of ea, Eau, eau, and yeo.

s.d: a shade of blue tinged with green
(uncountable) Water (as a compound).
(uncountable) A shade of colour, usually a mix of blue and green similar to the colour turquoise.
x: Ms. Rockburne, with help from a team of artists, is working on a gargantuan mural of deep blues, shimmering aquas and luminous gold leaf that is headed for the American Embassy in Kingston, Jamaica.

s.d: Of a greenish-blue colour.

aqua fortis.e: Learned borrowing from Latin aqua fortis (literally “strong water”).

s.d: acid used especially in the production of fertilizers and explosives and rocket fuels
(uncountable) A corrosive liquor made of saltpeter, serving as a solvent for dissolving silver and all other metals except gold.
(dated, dialectal, uncountable) Any strong and potentially dangerous alcoholic drink.
x: this man’s whiskey ain’t Red Eye, it ain’t Chain Lightnin’ either, it’s regular Agur-forty, and there isn’t a man living can stand a glass and keep his senses.
“Watkey” [vodka] is, in fact, aquafortis, and more injurious than any other spirit.

s.d: (archaic, uncountable) Synonym of nitric acid.

aqua regia.e: Learned borrowing from Latin aqua rēgia (literally “royal water”), so named because it is one of the few solvents capable of dissolving noble metals.

s.d: a yellow fuming corrosive mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acid that dissolves metals (including gold)
(archaic, uncountable) A mixture of three parts concentrated hydrochloric acid to one part concentrated nitric acid, named for its ability to dissolve gold.

aqua vitae.e: From Medieval Latin aqua vītae directly and via Middle English aqua vite and French eau-de-vie, from aqua (“water”) and vītae (“of life”). Doublet of aquavit and akvavit. Compare eau de vie, whisky, whiskey, and water of life from the same source.

s.d: strong distilled liquor or brandy
(uncountable) An aqueous solution of alcohol typically prepared by distilling wine.
(archaic, uncountable) A concentrated aqueous solution of ethanol.
(archaic, uncountable) Synonym of ardent spirits, particularly cognac and other French brandy.
x:
Ile ſooner truſt an Iriſhman vvith my
 Aquauita bottle, Sir Hu our parſon vvith my cheeſe,
 A theefe to vvalk my ambling gelding, thẽ my vvife
 VVith her ſelfe […]

x: Finally, sturgeon aquaculture would create a sustainable industry […]

aqualung.e: Aqualung was the original name for the first open-circuit SCUBA diving equipment by Emile Gagnan and Jacques Cousteau in 1943. From aqua- + lung.

s.d: a device (trade name Aqua-Lung) that lets divers breathe under water; scuba is an acronym for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus
A piece of equipment consisting of an oxygen tank and breathing apparatus used by divers to allow them to breathe underwater.
To scuba dive.

a shade of blue tinged with green

Of a bluish-green colour.
an underwater swimmer equipped with a face mask and foot fins and either a snorkel or an air cylinder
a skilled worker who can live in underwater installations and participate in scientific research
An underwater explorer.

aquaplane.e:
PIE word
 *h₂ékʷeh₂
The noun is derived from aqua- (prefix meaning ‘water’) + plane (“flat or level surface”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”)).
The verb is derived from the noun, and is analysable as aqua- + plane (“to glide; to soar; to skim a water surface”).

s.d: a board that is pulled by a speedboat as a person stands on it and skims over the top of the water
A board on which a person stands to ride for leisure which is pulled on a water surface by a motorboat.
rise up onto a thin film of water between the tires and road so that there is no more contact with the road
x: the car aquaplaned

s.d: ride on an aquaplane
To ride for leisure standing up on a board pulled on a water surface by a motorboat.
x: She waved her arm—a significant and imperative signal—but she realised, almost as she did it, that there was scant chance of any one aquaplaning at thirty or forty kilometres an hour looking to the right or to the left.

s.d: (UK) Of a car or other road vehicle: to lose traction with the road due to the vehicle's tyres sliding on a film of water on the road.
x: So much water. They were held up by it, the tyres skating over a film of rain. Aquaplaning. Flying his sister’s fancy car through the wet air. Touching nothing.

A tank, often made of glass, for keeping live fish or other aquatic animals.
A public place where live fish and other aquatic animals are exhibited.

x: In such a cistern the present and other hardy aquatics may be grown with success.

s.d: relating to or consisting of or being in water
x: an aquatic environment

s.d: operating or living or growing in water
x: boats are aquatic vehicles
water lilies are aquatic plants

wading and swimming and diving birds of either fresh or salt water
ferns that grow in water
whales and dolphins, manatees and dugongs, walruses, seals
a plant that grows partly or wholly in water whether rooted in the mud, as a lotus, or floating without anchorage, as the water hyacinth
animal living wholly or chiefly in or on water
sports that involve bodies of water
(plural-only) Sports involving water.
an etching made by a process that makes it resemble a water color
a method of etching that imitates the broad washes of a water color
A form of etching with acid on a plate partially covered with varnish that produces a print somewhat resembling a watercolour.
x: Aquatint is a laborious process that involves acids and resistants and emphasizes tone over line.

s.d: An etching or print made using this method.
x: Been thinking of my grandfather, whose wayward brilliance skipped my father’s generation. Once, he showed me an aquatint of a certain Siamese temple.

s.d: etch in aquatint
To make such etchings.

aquavit.e: From Swedish and Danish akvavit and Norwegian akevitt, from Medieval Latin aqua vitae (“water of life”). Doublet of aqua vitae and akvavit. Compare eau de vie, whisky, whiskey, and water of life from the same source.

s.d: Scandinavian liquor usually flavored with caraway seeds

(uncountable) A Scandinavian liquor distilled from potato or grain mash to about 40% ABV and typically flavored with anise, although caraway seeds, fennel, dill, and other spices and herbs are also used.

An artificial channel that is constructed to convey water from one location to another.
A structure carrying water over a river or depression, especially an ancient structure.
x: All the years he’d been down there in the traffic he’d taken this aqueduct for just another bridge, nothing to tell you that canal boats and waterfowl were being carried along above your head.

s.d: A structure conveying fluid, such as the cerebral aqueduct or vestibular aqueduct.
a canal connecting the third and fourth ventricles

aqueous.e: Formed from Latin aqua + -ous (or from Medieval Latin aqueus), partly the analogy of Middle French aqueux (itself actually from Latin aquosus). Or based on the analogy of Latin terreus from terra.

s.d: similar to or containing or dissolved in water
x: aqueous solutions

s.d: produced by the action of water
Of or relating to water.
Consisting mostly of water. Often used in the expression "aqueous solution".
x: It was dissolved in distilled water to prepare the exact aqueous dose (900 mg Kg −1 body weight) for intragastrical injection [ 9 ].

s.d: the limpid fluid within the eyeball between the cornea and the lens
the limpid fluid within the eyeball between the cornea and the lens

a solution in water

s.d: a technique of growing plants (without soil) in water containing dissolved nutrients

x: Frank's aquiline nose jutted out from underneath his glasses.
